title: Salvation Is for Ever Nigh
description: Salvation Is for Ever Nigh in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 85, part 2, headed “Salvation by Christ”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sal-va-tion is for ev-er nigh The souls that fear and trust the Lord; And grace de-scend-ing from on high, Fresh hopes of glo-ry shall af-ford.

lines: The souls that fear and trust the Lord;
And grace descending from on high,
Fresh hopes of glory shall afford.
Mercy and truth on earth are met,
Since Christ the Lord came down from heaven;
Justice is pleas'd, and peace is given.
Now truth and honour shall abound,
And heavenly influence bless the ground
To give us free access to God;
Our wandering feet shall stray no more,
But mark his steps and keep the road.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
